title: Engineering exact mobility edges in quasiperiodic Aharonov-Bohm chains
authors: Hai-Ying Cui, Yi-Cong Yu, Xiaoming Cai
abstract: We investigate localization phenomena and exact mobility edges in a quasiperiodic Aharonov-Bohm chain, where the 1D canonical diagonal and off-diagonal Aubry-André-Harper models are laterally coupled to an auxiliary sublattice threaded by a synthetic magnetic flux. By analytically computing the Lyapunov exponent via Avila's global theory of one-frequency Schrödinger operators, we derive exact expressions for mobility edges. In the diagonal limit, the coupling to the auxiliary sublattice generates hyperbolic mobility edges that exhibit a sign-changing divergence and can be continuously tuned by the magnetic flux. In the off-diagonal regime, the interference between quasiperiodic hopping and indirect tunneling through the auxiliary sublattice gives rise to exact anomalous mobility edges that separate critical and extended states. Critical states and anomalous mobility edges emerge even in the absence of incommensurately distributed zeros in the hopping modulation, a behavior distinct from that of conventional off-diagonal models. Our results establish a rigorous theoretical framework for engineering controllable mobility edges, with the synthetic flux providing a tunable experimental knob that paves the way for realizations in platforms such as superconducting quantum circuits and photonic waveguides.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework to precisely engineer mobility edges in quasiperiodic Aharonov-Bohm chains. By coupling Aubry-André-Harper models with a synthetic magnetic flux, the authors derive exact expressions for these edges. This tunability makes the model highly relevant for designing quantum devices in superconducting circuits or photonic waveguides.
main_problem: The paper investigates localization phenomena and derives exact expressions for mobility edges in a quasiperiodic Aharonov-Bohm chain.
main_result: The authors establish a rigorous framework for engineering controllable mobility edges, showing that anomalous mobility edges can emerge even without conventional disorder features.
method: The analysis involves analytically computing the Lyapunov exponent using Avila’s global theory of one-frequency Schrödinger operators.
model_or_system: The system is a quasiperiodic Aharonov-Bohm chain, modeled as a lateral coupling of 1D diagonal and off-diagonal Aubry-André-Harper models to an auxiliary sublattice threaded by a synthetic magnetic flux.
key_observables: Mobility Edges (MEs) and Anomalous Mobility Edges (AMEs), and the Lyapunov Exponent ($\gamma$).
important_parameters: Magnetic flux ($\phi$), modulation strengths ($W, V$), and the quasiperiodicity parameter ($ eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the AB geometry and the application of Avila’s global theory for exact results.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the chain and show how MEs evolve as parameters like modulation strength ($W$) and flux ($\phi$) are varied.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the coupled Hamiltonian, deriving an effective eigenequation, calculating the Lyapunov exponent using advanced theory, and then analyzing the resulting MEs in both diagonal and off-diagonal limits.
why_interesting: The ability to analytically derive exact, tunable mobility edges using a synthetic flux provides a powerful theoretical tool for designing quantum transport in engineered platforms.
